1709	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
1710	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
1711	        for robot in self.robots.values():
1712	            if robot.task_id is None:
1713	                continue
1714	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
1715	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
1716	                task.picked_up = True

1718	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
1719	        # Robots whose task finishes during this tick -- whether after driving
1720	        # onto the dropoff or without moving at all (in-place completion, or a
1721	        # map-paused task recovered into a zero-step route). Such a robot must
1722	        # still stand on the delivery cell when this tick ends: the replay's
1723	        # first-completion evidence and the checkpoint loader both require it
1724	        # there. It is therefore never asked to yield and never counts as able
1725	        # to vacate its cell for the rest of this tick. The set only lives for
1726	        # this tick -- on the next tick the robot is an ordinary parked robot
1727	        # again and yields normally, so finishing never turns the dropoff into
1728	        # a permanent reservation.
1729	        completed_now: set[str] = set()
1730	
1731	        def mark_finished(robot: Robot) -> None:
1732	            completed_now.add(robot.robot_id)
1733	
1734	        self._confirm_pickups()
1735	        self._recover_paused_tasks(on_completion=mark_finished)
1736	        self.assign_tasks()
1737	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
1738	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
1739	        self._confirm_pickups()
1740	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1741	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
1742	        moved: list[str] = []
1743	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
1744	        # Robots that stopped this tick on another robot. Only the set of
1745	        # identities is kept: which robot each one saw mid-tick is not
1746	        # trusted -- the end-of-tick layout settles the actual blocker (see
1747	        # :meth:`_settle_traffic_waits`).
1748	        waited: set[str] = set()
1749	
1750	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
1751	            del occupied[robot.position]
1752	            robot.position = destination
1753	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
1754	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
1755	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
1756	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
1757	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
1758	
1759	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
1760	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
1761	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
1762	                continue
1763	            if robot.robot_id in completed_now:
1764	                # Its task finished earlier in this very tick and the robot is
1765	                # parked on the dropoff: it must end the tick there, so it
1766	                # neither drives for itself nor yields for anyone this tick.
1767	                continue
1768	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
1769	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1770	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
1771	                continue
1772	            if not robot.route:
1773	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot, on_completion=mark_finished)
1774	                continue
1775	            destination = robot.route[0]
1776	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
1777	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
1778	                # The same feasibility/route/pause rule an accepted edit and
1779	                # step-start recovery use settles it here too.
1780	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
1781	                    self._refresh_bound_task_route(task, robot)
1782	                continue
1783	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
1784	            if blocker_id is None:
1785	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
1786	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
1787	                relocate(robot, destination)
1788	                robot.route.pop(0)
1789	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot, on_completion=mark_finished)
1790	                continue
1791	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
1792	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
1793	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
1794	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids and blocker_id not in completed_now:
1795	                if blocker.task_id is None and not blocker.route:
1796	                    # Truly parked blocker: no bound task and no remaining
1797	                    # route. Ask it to yield onto a free side cell, then take
1798	                    # over the cell it vacated. A taskless robot that still has
1799	                    # a remaining route is not parked: it drives that route
1800	                    # cell by cell like any other moving robot and is never
1801	                    # pushed off it for a requester. A robot that finished a
1802	                    # task earlier this tick looks parked but stays on the
1803	                    # dropoff until the tick ends (see ``completed_now``).
1804	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
1805	                    if side is not None:
1806	                        relocate(blocker, side)
1807	                        relocate(robot, destination)
1808	                        robot.route.pop(0)
1809	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot, on_completion=mark_finished)
1810	                        continue
1811	                if blocker.route:
1812	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
1813	                    if (
1814	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
1815	                        and ahead not in occupied
1816	                        and ahead not in reserved
1817	                    ):
1818	                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
1819	                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
1820	                        waited.add(robot.robot_id)
1821	                        continue
1822	            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
1823	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
1824	            side = self._self_sidestep(
1825	                robot,
1826	                task,
1827	                occupied,
1828	                reserved,
1829	                frozenset(moved_ids),
1830	                cannot_yield=frozenset(completed_now),
1831	            )
1832	            if side is not None:
1833	                cell, route = side
1834	                relocate(robot, cell)
1835	                robot.route = route
1836	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot, on_completion=mark_finished)
1837	                continue
1838	            waited.add(robot.robot_id)
1839	        self._settle_traffic_waits(waited)
1840	        self.tick += 1
1841	        event: dict[str, object] = {
1842	            "type": "tick",
1843	            "tick": self.tick,
1844	            "moved": moved,
1845	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
1846	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
1847	        }
1848	        self.replay.append(event)
1849	        # Hand back an independent copy: trimming or editing the returned
1850	        # frame must never rewrite the history recorded here.
1851	        return copy.deepcopy(event)

1854	        self,
1855	        robot: Robot,

1917	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
1918	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
1919	
1920	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
1921	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
1922	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
1923	        raise :class:`OSError`.
1924	        """
1925	        document = {
1926	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
1927	            "grid": {
1928	                "width": self.grid.width,
1929	                "height": self.grid.height,
1930	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
1931	            },
1932	            "base_grid": {
1933	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
1934	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
1935	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
1936	            },
1937	            "tick": self.tick,
1938	            "robots": [
1939	                {
1940	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
1941	                    "position": list(robot.position),
1942	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
1943	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
1944	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
1945	                }
1946	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
1947	            ],
1948	            "tasks": [
1949	                {
1950	                    "task_id": task.task_id,
1951	                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
1952	                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
1953	                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
1954	                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
1955	                    "completed": task.completed,
1956	                }
1957	                for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)
1958	            ],
1959	            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
1960	            "map_changes": copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes),
1961	            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
1962	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
1963	        }
1964	        payload = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
1965	
1966	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))) or os.curdir
1967	        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
1968	        try:
1969	            handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
1970	            try:
1971	                handle.write(payload)
1972	                handle.flush()
1973	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
1974	            finally:
1975	                handle.close()
1976	            os.replace(tmp_name, path)
1977	            self._fsync_directory(directory)
1978	        except BaseException:
1979	            # After a successful replace the temp name is already gone.
1980	            try:
1981	                os.unlink(tmp_name)
1982	            except OSError:
1983	                pass
1984	            raise

1988	        try:
1989	            dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
1990	        except OSError:
1991	            return
1992	        try:
1993	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
1994	        except OSError:
1995	            pass
1996	        finally:
1997	            os.close(dir_fd)

2000	    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FleetSimulator:
2001	        """Load an independent simulator instance from *path*.
2002	
2003	        The returned simulator shares no mutable state with the file or any
2004	        other loaded instance. Invalid checkpoint content raises
2005	        :class:`ValueError` explaining the reason; read/permission failures
2006	        propagate as :class:`OSError`.

2009	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
2010	                text = handle.read()

2012	            raise
2013	        try:
2014	            data = json.loads(text)

2017	        return cls._from_checkpoint(data)

2019	    @classmethod
2020	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
2021	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
2022	            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")
2023	
2024	        version = data.get("version")
2025	        if not _is_int(version):
2026	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
2027	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
2028	            raise ValueError(
2029	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
2030	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
2031	            )
2032	
2033	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
2034	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
2035	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
2036	
2037	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
2038	        paused: set[str] = set()
2039	        if version == 1:
2040	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
2041	            base_grid = grid
2042	            # Version 1 has no change history: every blocked waypoint keeps
2043	            # being judged purely against the saved grid, exactly as before.
2044	            history_closed: frozenset[Position] = frozenset()
2045	        else:
2046	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
2047	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
2048	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
2049	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
2050	            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
2051	                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")
2052	            cls._validate_map_history(base_grid, grid, map_changes)
2053	            history_closed = cls._history_closed_cells(base_grid, map_changes)
2054	
2055	        robots: list[Robot] = []
2056	        for record in robot_records:
2057	            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
2058	            if not grid.traversable(position):
2059	                raise ValueError(
2060	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
2061	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
2062	                )
2063	            # Walkability uses the very same shared cell-by-cell rule as
2064	            # direct construction (strict JSON list format and checkpoint
2065	            # wording preserved); the task pickup/dropoff rules are a separate
2066	            # check below. The only relaxation checkpoint recovery adds over
2067	            # direct construction is for a robot with no bound task whose
2068	            # preset route waits before a cell the recorded edits closed: such
2069	            # a waypoint is unobstructed on the base map and still blocked on
2070	            # the saved one, so the route keeps it instead of being rejected
2071	            # as an illegal walk. A bound task route, an initial obstacle and
2072	            # anything the history cannot explain stay strict.
2073	            allowed_blocked = (
2074	                history_closed
2075	                if record["task_id"] is None
2076	                else frozenset()
2077	            )
2078	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = _validate_route_walk(
2079	                grid,
2080	                position,
2081	                record["route"],
2082	                robot_id=record["robot_id"],
2083	                checkpoint=True,
2084	                blocked_cells=allowed_blocked,
2085	            )
2086	            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
2087	            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
2088	                raise ValueError(
2089	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
2090	                    "non-negative integer"
2091	                )
2092	            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))
2093	
2094	        tasks: list[Task] = []
2095	        for record in task_records:
2096	            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
2097	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
2098	            tasks.append(
2099	                Task(
2100	                    record["task_id"],
2101	                    pickup,

        """Side cells a busy robot could escape to, with their replanned routes.

        Only cells off every other robot's planned route that keep the robot's
        task reachable are offered, in deterministic neighbour order. Whether
        such a cell is a genuine way out -- or just moves the robot aside for
        one tick before it is driven back onto the same blocked corridor -- is
        judged by the caller as it scans the candidates.
        """
        for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
            robot, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
        ):
            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=side_cell)
            if route is not None:
                yield side_cell, route

    def _can_vacate(
        self,
        blocker: Robot,
        requester: Robot,
        occupied: dict[Position, str],
        reserved: dict[Position, str],
        checking: frozenset[str],
        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
    ) -> bool:
        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.

        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots already on the
        dependency chain (including robots that used their one move of this
        tick), so meeting one again closes a cyclic dependency -- a head-on
        deadlock, or the requester itself -- and never proves an exit merely
        because every robot on the cycle still carries a route. It also names
        robots that finished a task earlier in this tick: they look parked but
        must end the tick standing on their delivery cell, so they never
        vacate for anyone.
        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
        the blocker's own route does).

        A task-bound blocker's own side step is judged by the same standard as
        the requester's retreat: it counts as leaving only when the replanned
        route from the side cell does not lead straight back through the cell
        being vacated into another robot that cannot get out of the way
        either. A side cell the blocker must leave again on the next tick to
        re-face the very same unyielding jam further down the corridor is no
        way out, so it never justifies the retreat behind it.

        The follow chain can run through an arbitrarily long legal queue, so
        the search is an explicit stack rather than Python recursion: a queue
        of twelve hundred robots ending at a parked robot with no side cell
        must report "cannot vacate" from a normal ``step()`` instead of
        raising :class:`RecursionError`. Each frame is
        ``(robot, occupied, checking, blocked_path, resume)``: a nested
        hypothetical (the blocker having stepped aside) works with its own
        layout and no-go cells, so both travel with the frame. *resume* is
        ``None`` on a frame's first visit and afterwards holds the robot's
        not-yet-tried side-exit candidates as a stateful iterator. A frame
        examined for the first time first tries the free-waypoint and
        follow-chain rules; only when the chain ahead comes back empty does it
        resume at its own side-cell scan, continuing exactly where that scan
        stopped -- the order the single recursive call imposed.
        """
        frame = (blocker, occupied, checking, blocked_path, None)
        stack: list[
            tuple[
                Robot,
                dict[Position, str],
                frozenset[str],
                frozenset[Position],
                Iterator[tuple[Position, list[Position]]] | None,
            ]
        ] = [frame]
        while stack:
            current, cur_occupied, cur_checking, cur_blocked_path, resume = stack.pop()
            if current.robot_id in cur_checking:
                # The chain has folded back onto a robot it already depends
                # on: a cycle cannot vacate itself. The frame that followed
                # this one simply resumes with its own side-cell options.
                continue
            task = self.tasks[current.task_id] if current.task_id is not None else None
            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
                continue
            if not current.route:
                if task is not None:
                    # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this
                    # tick; it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
                    continue
                # A parked robot (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
                # yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; it does
                # so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
                # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
                # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
                # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
                side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(current, requester, cur_occupied, reserved)
                if side is not None and side not in cur_blocked_path:
                    return True
                continue
            if resume is None:
                ahead = current.route[0]
                if (
                    self.grid.traversable(ahead)
                    and ahead not in cur_occupied
                    and ahead not in reserved
                ):
                    return True
                # A robot id may be any string, including "": only a missing
                # entry (None) means the cell is empty, never a falsy id.
                occupant_id = cur_occupied.get(ahead)
                if occupant_id is None:
                    occupant_id = reserved.get(ahead)
                if (
                    occupant_id is not None
                    and occupant_id != current.robot_id
                    and occupant_id not in cur_checking
                ):
                    # The robot could follow the occupant once that robot
                    # vacates its cell this same tick. This frame resumes with
                    # its side-cell scan only after the chain ahead proves it
                    # cannot clear, mirroring the recursive call order.
                    stack.append(
                        (
                            current,
                            cur_occupied,
                            cur_checking,
                            cur_blocked_path,
                            self._side_exit_cells(
                                current, task, cur_occupied, reserved, cur_blocked_path
                            )
                            if task is not None
                            else iter(()),
                        )
                    )
                    stack.append(
                        (
                            self.robots[occupant_id],
                            cur_occupied,
                            cur_checking | {current.robot_id},
                            cur_blocked_path,
                            None,
                        )
                    )
                    continue
                resume = (
                    self._side_exit_cells(
                        current, task, cur_occupied, reserved, cur_blocked_path
                    )
                    if task is not None
                    else iter(())
                )
            if task is None:
                # A taskless robot that still drives a remaining route never
                # sidesteps off it -- not even to unblock a requester -- so a side
                # cell cannot count as a way out for it.
                continue
            # Otherwise the task-bound blocker might sidestep onto a free side
            # cell itself, but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has
            # to use -- parking there only moves the blockage.
            chained = False
            for side_cell, route in resume:
                if not route or route[0] != current.position:
                    # A genuine exit: the robot drives on elsewhere instead of
                    # returning onto the cell it just vacated.
                    return True
                # The replanned route leads straight back through the cell
                # being vacated. That still counts as leaving when the way
                # back is clear, or when whoever holds it can clear out in
                # turn -- but not when the robot would re-face a jam that has
                # no exit of its own, because then the side step is undone on
                # the next tick with nothing gained.
                hyp_occupied = dict(cur_occupied)
                del hyp_occupied[current.position]
                hyp_occupied[side_cell] = current.robot_id
                holder_id: str | None = None
                for cell in route[1:]:
                    # Same empty-string rule as the follow chain above: a
                    # robot named "" still holds its cell.
                    holder = hyp_occupied.get(cell)
                    if holder is None:
                        holder = reserved.get(cell)
                    if holder is not None and holder != current.robot_id:
                        holder_id = holder
                        break
                if holder_id is None:
                    return True
                if holder_id in cur_checking:
                    continue
                stack.append(
                    (current, cur_occupied, cur_checking, cur_blocked_path, resume)
                )
                stack.append(
                    (
                        self.robots[holder_id],
                        hyp_occupied,
                        cur_checking | {current.robot_id},
                        frozenset(route),
                        None,
                    )
                )
                chained = True
                break
            if chained:
                continue
        return False

    def _settle_traffic_waits(self, waited: Iterable[str]) -> None:
        """Settle this tick's waits against the end-of-tick layout.

        *waited* names every robot that stopped this tick purely because
        another robot held its next waypoint at the time. That mid-tick
        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
        The shared :func:`_traffic_blockers` fact on the settled layout then
        decides everything, so a record survives only when the robot actually
        waited (is in *waited*), did not move, was not paused and still faces a
        robot on its next cell; the recorded blocker is whichever robot holds
        that cell at tick end. Any other outcome -- the robot moved, its task
        paused, or the way ahead cleared -- removes the entry. A wait that
        continues without a free tick in between keeps accumulating even when
        the blocker changes identity; once interrupted, a later blockage
        starts a fresh count at one.
        """
        blockers = _traffic_blockers(self.robots, self._paused_robots())
        settled: dict[str, tuple[str, int]] = {}
        for robot_id in waited:
            blocker_id = blockers.get(robot_id)
            if blocker_id is None:
                continue
            previous = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
            ticks = 1 if previous is None else previous[1] + 1
            settled[robot_id] = (blocker_id, ticks)
        self._traffic_waits = settled

    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.

        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
        add to one; but it can end one, and the same shared fact settles it as
        a normal tick (:func:`_traffic_blockers`). A robot whose task just
        paused on unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot
        whose replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is
        not blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
        """
        blockers = _traffic_blockers(self.robots, self._paused_robots())
        for robot_id, (blocker_id, _ticks) in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
            if blockers.get(robot_id) != blocker_id:
                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]

    def _paused_robots(self) -> frozenset[str]:
        """Robots whose bound task is paused by map unreachability."""
        return frozenset(
            robot.robot_id
            for robot in self.robots.values()
            if robot.task_id is not None
            and robot.task_id in self.paused_tasks
        )

    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
        # Fresh containers in robot-id order: a caller that edits a returned
        # report -- or the one-element ``blocked_by`` list -- can never reach
        # the simulator's own records or change a later judgement.
        return [
            {
                "robot_id": robot_id,
                "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
                "ticks": ticks,
            }
            for robot_id, (blocker_id, ticks) in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
        ]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Normal execution
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest available robot using stable tie breaks.

        Only a robot with no bound task *and* no remaining route is available:
        a taskless robot still driving a preset route keeps that route and is
        never selected, even when it is the closest to the pickup -- being
        temporarily blocked by traffic does not count as having finished the
        route either. Skipping such a robot never touches its position,
        mileage, cargo state or remaining waypoints, and never makes other
        tasks wait: the next available robot is chosen by the usual shortest
        feasible route length with the robot id string as tie break.
        """
        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
            for robot in self.robots.values():
                if not robot.idle or robot.route:
                    continue
                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
                if route is None:
                    continue
                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
            if not choices:
                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
                # not block assignment of other tasks.
                continue
            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
            robot.task_id = task.task_id
            robot.route = route
            task.assigned_robot = robot_id

    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
        for robot in self.robots.values():
            if robot.task_id is None:
                continue
            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
                task.picked_up = True

    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        # Robots whose task finishes during this tick -- whether after driving
        # onto the dropoff or without moving at all (in-place completion, or a
        # map-paused task recovered into a zero-step route). Such a robot must
        # still stand on the delivery cell when this tick ends: the replay's
        # first-completion evidence and the checkpoint loader both require it
        # there. It is therefore never asked to yield and never counts as able
        # to vacate its cell for the rest of this tick. The set only lives for
        # this tick -- on the next tick the robot is an ordinary parked robot
        # again and yields normally, so finishing never turns the dropoff into
        # a permanent reservation.
        completed_now: set[str] = set()

        def mark_finished(robot: Robot) -> None:
            completed_now.add(robot.robot_id)

        self._confirm_pickups()
        self._recover_paused_tasks(on_completion=mark_finished)
        self.assign_tasks()
        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
        self._confirm_pickups()
        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
        moved: list[str] = []
        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
        # Robots that stopped this tick on another robot. Only the set of
        # identities is kept: which robot each one saw mid-tick is not
        # trusted -- the end-of-tick layout settles the actual blocker (see
        # :meth:`_settle_traffic_waits`).
        waited: set[str] = set()

        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
            del occupied[robot.position]
            robot.position = destination
            robot.distance_travelled += 1
            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)

        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
                continue
            if robot.robot_id in completed_now:
                # Its task finished earlier in this very tick and the robot is
                # parked on the dropoff: it must end the tick there, so it
                # neither drives for itself nor yields for anyone this tick.
                continue
            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
                continue
            if not robot.route:
                self._finish_if_arrived(robot, on_completion=mark_finished)
                continue
            destination = robot.route[0]
            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
                # The same feasibility/route/pause rule an accepted edit and
                # step-start recovery use settles it here too.
                if task is not None and not task.completed:
                    self._refresh_bound_task_route(task, robot)
                continue
            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
            if blocker_id is None:
                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
                relocate(robot, destination)
                robot.route.pop(0)
                self._finish_if_arrived(robot, on_completion=mark_finished)
                continue
            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
            if blocker_id not in moved_ids and blocker_id not in completed_now:
                if blocker.task_id is None and not blocker.route:
                    # Truly parked blocker: no bound task and no remaining
                    # route. Ask it to yield onto a free side cell, then take
                    # over the cell it vacated. A taskless robot that still has
                    # a remaining route is not parked: it drives that route
                    # cell by cell like any other moving robot and is never
                    # pushed off it for a requester. A robot that finished a
                    # task earlier this tick looks parked but stays on the
                    # dropoff until the tick ends (see ``completed_now``).
                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
                    if side is not None:
                        relocate(blocker, side)
                        relocate(robot, destination)
                        robot.route.pop(0)
                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot, on_completion=mark_finished)
                        continue
                if blocker.route:
                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
                    if (
                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
                        and ahead not in occupied
                        and ahead not in reserved
                    ):
                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
                        waited.add(robot.robot_id)
                        continue
            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
            side = self._self_sidestep(
                robot,
                task,
                occupied,
                reserved,
                frozenset(moved_ids),
                cannot_yield=frozenset(completed_now),
            )
            if side is not None:
                cell, route = side
                relocate(robot, cell)
                robot.route = route
                self._finish_if_arrived(robot, on_completion=mark_finished)
                continue
            waited.add(robot.robot_id)
        self._settle_traffic_waits(waited)
        self.tick += 1
        event: dict[str, object] = {
            "type": "tick",
            "tick": self.tick,
            "moved": moved,
            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
        }
        self.replay.append(event)
        # Hand back an independent copy: trimming or editing the returned
        # frame must never rewrite the history recorded here.
        return copy.deepcopy(event)

    def _finish_if_arrived(
        self,
        robot: Robot,
        *,
        on_completion: Callable[[Robot], None] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if robot.task_id is None:
            return
        task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
        if task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
            return
        if robot.position == task.pickup:
            task.picked_up = True
        if task.picked_up and robot.position == task.dropoff and not robot.route:
            task.completed = True
            self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
            robot.task_id = None
            if on_completion is not None:
                on_completion(robot)

    def metrics(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        completed = sum(task.completed for task in self.tasks.values())
        return {
            "ticks": self.tick,
            "tasks_total": len(self.tasks),
            "tasks_completed": completed,
            "tasks_paused": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
            "completion_ratio": completed / len(self.tasks) if self.tasks else 1.0,
            "distance_total": sum(robot.distance_travelled for robot in self.robots.values()),
            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
        }

    def status(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Obstacles, map-unreachability pauses and per-robot traffic waits."""
        return {
            "tick": self.tick,
            "width": self.grid.width,
            "height": self.grid.height,
            "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
        }

    def map_change_history(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
        """Effective time, added/removed cells and order of every actual edit."""
        return copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes)

    def snapshot(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        return {
            "tick": self.tick,
            "robots": [asdict(robot) for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)],
            "tasks": [asdict(task) for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)],
            "metrics": self.metrics(),
            # An independent copy of the history: later steps and map edits
            # extend the simulator's own replay without growing snapshots
            # already handed out, and edits to a returned snapshot never
            # reach the recorded history.
            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Checkpoint persistence
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.

        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
        raise :class:`OSError`.
        """
        document = {
            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
            "grid": {
                "width": self.grid.width,
                "height": self.grid.height,
                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
            },
            "base_grid": {
                "width": self.base_grid.width,
                "height": self.base_grid.height,
                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
            },
            "tick": self.tick,
            "robots": [
                {
                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
                    "position": list(robot.position),
                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
                }
                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
            ],
            "tasks": [
                {
                    "task_id": task.task_id,
                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
                    "completed": task.completed,
                }
                for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)
            ],
            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
            "map_changes": copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes),
            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
        }
        payload = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")

        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))) or os.curdir
        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
        try:
            handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
            try:
                handle.write(payload)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
            finally:
                handle.close()
            os.replace(tmp_name, path)
            self._fsync_directory(directory)
        except BaseException:
            # After a successful replace the temp name is already gone.
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp_name)
            except OSError:
                pass
            raise

    @staticmethod
    def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
        try:
            dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
        except OSError:
            return
        try:
            os.fsync(dir_fd)
        except OSError:
            pass
        finally:
            os.close(dir_fd)

    @classmethod
    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FleetSimulator:
        """Load an independent simulator instance from *path*.

        The returned simulator shares no mutable state with the file or any
        other loaded instance. Invalid checkpoint content raises
        :class:`ValueError` explaining the reason; read/permission failures
        propagate as :class:`OSError`.
        """
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                text = handle.read()
        except OSError:
            raise
        try:
            data = json.loads(text)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is not valid JSON: {exc.msg}") from exc
        return cls._from_checkpoint(data)

    @classmethod
    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")

        version = data.get("version")
        if not _is_int(version):
            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
            )

        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)

        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        paused: set[str] = set()
        if version == 1:
            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
            base_grid = grid
            # Version 1 has no change history: every blocked waypoint keeps
            # being judged purely against the saved grid, exactly as before.
            history_closed: frozenset[Position] = frozenset()
        else:
            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")
            cls._validate_map_history(base_grid, grid, map_changes)
            history_closed = cls._history_closed_cells(base_grid, map_changes)

        robots: list[Robot] = []
        for record in robot_records:
            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
            if not grid.traversable(position):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
                )
            # Walkability uses the very same shared cell-by-cell rule as
            # direct construction (strict JSON list format and checkpoint
            # wording preserved); the task pickup/dropoff rules are a separate
            # check below. The only relaxation checkpoint recovery adds over
            # direct construction is for a robot with no bound task whose
            # preset route waits before a cell the recorded edits closed: such
            # a waypoint is unobstructed on the base map and still blocked on
            # the saved one, so the route keeps it instead of being rejected
            # as an illegal walk. A bound task route, an initial obstacle and
            # anything the history cannot explain stay strict.
            allowed_blocked = (
                history_closed
                if record["task_id"] is None
                else frozenset()
            )
            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = _validate_route_walk(
                grid,
                position,
                record["route"],
                robot_id=record["robot_id"],
                checkpoint=True,
                blocked_cells=allowed_blocked,
            )
            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
                    "non-negative integer"
                )
            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))

        tasks: list[Task] = []
        for record in task_records:
            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
            tasks.append(
                Task(
                    record["task_id"],
                    pickup,
                    dropoff,
                    record["assigned_robot"],
                    record["picked_up"],
                    record["completed"],
                )
            )

        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}

        # Ownership and the completed-task history are judged with the exact
        # rules direct construction uses -- mutual bindings for work in
        # progress, a collected task that may never lack its carrier, and a
        # finished task that must keep its picked-up mark and historical owner
        # -- so a checkpoint can never load a completion that direct
        # construction would have rejected (or vice versa).
        cls._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)

        cls._validate_paused_state(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id, grid)
        cls._validate_active_task_routes(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id)
        traffic_waits = cls._load_traffic_waits(data, robot_by_id)

        replay_change_frames = cls._replay_map_change_frames(replay)
        if replay_change_frames != map_changes:
            raise ValueError("replay map-change frames do not match 'map_changes' history")

        simulator = cls(grid, robots, tasks, _routes_prevalidated=True)
        simulator.base_grid = base_grid
        simulator.tick = tick
        simulator.replay = copy.deepcopy(replay)
        simulator.map_changes = copy.deepcopy(map_changes)
        simulator._map_sequence = len(map_changes)
        simulator.paused_tasks = set(paused)
        simulator._traffic_waits = traffic_waits
        # Completion history is judged before frame position plausibility so a
        # missing delivery robot is reported with the task-specific reason
        # (frame, task, robot) rather than the generic robot-id mismatch.
        cls._validate_replay_completion(replay, tick, task_by_id)
        # Version 1 has no edit history: its saved grid is the baseline and
        # applies to every tick frame. Version 2 replays the recorded changes
        # alongside the frames so each frame is judged against its contemporary
        # map.
        cls._validate_replay_positions(replay, tick, robot_by_id, base_grid, map_changes)
        return simulator

    @staticmethod
    def _require_field(data: Mapping[str, object], field_name: str) -> object:
        if field_name not in data:
            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is missing required field {field_name!r}")
        return data[field_name]

    @classmethod
    def _load_grid(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> GridMap:
        return cls._load_map_definition(
            data, "grid", map_label="grid", obstacle_label="obstacle"
        )

    @classmethod
    def _load_base_grid(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> GridMap:
        return cls._load_map_definition(
            data, "base_grid", map_label="base grid", obstacle_label="base obstacle"
        )

    @classmethod
    def _load_map_definition(
        cls,
        data: Mapping[str, object],
        field_name: str,
        *,
        map_label: str,
        obstacle_label: str,
    ) -> GridMap:
        """Validate one checkpoint map definition and build its grid.

        This is the single place that owns the map-definition rule shared by
        the current ``grid`` and the version 2 ``base_grid``, so a format or
        value rule never has to be changed in two places: the field must be an
        object with positive integer ``width``/``height`` (booleans are not
        integers) and an ``obstacles`` list of ``[x, y]`` integer pairs, each
        lying inside its own map. An empty obstacle list is legal, and a
        coordinate repeated within the list denotes a single obstacle. Nothing
        is coerced -- strings, floats and booleans are rejected, never
        converted -- and the file-format judgement is not relaxed just because
        a grid could be built from the values.

        The two definitions are validated independently and keep their own
        contents: neither map is ever copied from the other. Only the wording
        differs between the two entry points, via *map_label* (``grid`` /
        ``base grid``) and *obstacle_label* (``obstacle`` / ``base obstacle``),
        so an error still names the map and the exact dimension or obstacle
        entry at fault. Cross-definition rules -- matching dimensions and a
        history that replays the base grid onto the current one -- are checked
        separately afterwards and stay distinct rejection reasons.
        """
        raw = cls._require_field(data, field_name)
        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint field {field_name!r} must be an object")
        width = raw.get("width")
        height = raw.get("height")
        if not _is_int(width) or width <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint {map_label} width must be a positive integer"
            )
        if not _is_int(height) or height <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint {map_label} height must be a positive integer"
            )
        raw_obstacles = raw.get("obstacles")
        if not isinstance(raw_obstacles, list):
            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint {map_label} 'obstacles' must be a list")
        obstacles: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
        for index, cell in enumerate(raw_obstacles):
            obstacle = _as_pair(cell, f"{obstacle_label} entry {index}")
            if not (0 <= obstacle[0] < width and 0 <= obstacle[1] < height):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{obstacle_label} {list(obstacle)} lies outside the map"
                )
            obstacles.add(obstacle)
        try:
            return GridMap(width, height, frozenset(obstacles))
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid checkpoint {map_label}: {exc}") from exc

2368	    def _validate_map_history(
2369	        cls,
2370	        base_grid: GridMap,
2371	        saved_grid: GridMap,
2372	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
2373	    ) -> None:
2374	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
2375	        width, height = saved_grid.width, saved_grid.height

2377	            for key in ("added", "removed"):

2387	            for cell in added:

2389	                    raise ValueError(
2390	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} adds obstacle {list(cell)} "
2391	                        "that is already present according to the history"
2392	                    )
2393	            for cell in removed:
2394	                if cell not in obstacles:
2395	                    raise ValueError(
2396	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} removes obstacle {list(cell)} "
2397	                        "that is absent according to the history"
2398	                    )
2399	            obstacles |= added
2400	            obstacles -= removed

2402	            raise ValueError(
2403	                "the map reproduced from 'map_changes' does not match the saved grid"

2406	    @staticmethod
2407	    def _history_closed_cells(
2408	        base_grid: GridMap,
2409	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
2410	    ) -> frozenset[Position]:
2411	        """Cells open on the base map that the recorded edits net-close.
2412	
2413	        The change history is replayed from *base_grid* (its validity and
2414	        reproduction of the saved grid are checked separately by
2415	        :meth:`_validate_map_history`), and the result holds exactly the cells
2416	        a preset-route robot may legitimately still name while waiting: open
2417	        in the initial map, closed later by an accepted edit, and still closed
2418	        at save time. A cell closed and reopened before the save nets to open
2419	        and is therefore absent, as is every base-map obstacle.
2420	        """
2421	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
2422	        for frame in changes:
2423	            obstacles.update(tuple(cell) for cell in frame["added"])
2424	            obstacles.difference_update(tuple(cell) for cell in frame["removed"])
2425	        return frozenset(obstacles - set(base_grid.obstacles))

2473	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
2474	                raise ValueError(f"{context} must be an object")
2475	            robot_id = entry.get("robot_id")
2476	            if not isinstance(robot_id, str):

2484	                not isinstance(blocked_by, list)
2485	                or not blocked_by
2486	                or not all(isinstance(value, str) for value in blocked_by)

2489	                    f"{context} field 'blocked_by' must be a non-empty list of strings"

2563	    @staticmethod
2564	    def _validate_active_task_routes(
2565	        paused: set[str],
2566	        task_by_id: Mapping[str, Task],
2567	        robot_by_id: Mapping[str, Robot],
2568	    ) -> None:
2569	        """Reject routes that cannot finish the task each robot is bound to.
2570	
2571	        Traversability and adjacency are checked elsewhere. This enforces the
2572	        pickup/delivery business rules -- the very same waypoint requirement
2573	        :func:`_task_route_waypoints` plans with -- for tasks that are
2574	        assigned, unfinished and not paused by map unreachability: a non-empty
2575	        route must end at the dropoff, and a robot that has not collected yet
2576	        -- and is not already standing on the pickup cell -- must still pass
2577	        through the pickup. Passing the dropoff early changes nothing; the
2578	        route only has to reach the pickup and return, and saved avoidance
2579	        detours need not match a replanned shortest route. Empty routes are
2580	        legal only when no remaining waypoint is required: the loaded robot is
2581	        already at the dropoff, or position, pickup and dropoff all coincide
2582	        (the goods are collected on resume). Paused tasks keep their empty-route
2583	        exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not judged as work in
2584	        progress.
2585	        """

2587	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
2588	                continue
2589	            if task.task_id in paused:
2590	                # Map-unreachability pauses legitimately carry an empty route
2591	                # regardless of pickup state; the binding itself is all that
2592	                # must survive.
2593	                continue
2594	            robot = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
2595	            if robot is None or robot.task_id != task.task_id:
2596	                # Ownership mismatches of this kind are reported separately.
2597	                continue
2598	            route = robot.route
2599	            label = (
2600	                f"task {task.task_id!r} assigned to robot {robot.robot_id!r}"
2601	            )
2602	            required = _task_route_waypoints(robot.position, task)
2603	            if route:
2604	                if route[-1] != task.dropoff:
2605	                    raise ValueError(
2606	                        f"{label} has a remaining route that ends at "
2607	                        f"{list(route[-1])} instead of its dropoff "
2608	                        f"{list(task.dropoff)}"
2609	                    )
2610	                if task.pickup in required and task.pickup not in route:
2611	                    raise ValueError(
2612	                        f"{label} has not picked up the goods and its remaining "
2613	                        f"route never reaches the pickup point "
2614	                        f"{list(task.pickup)} on the way to its dropoff "
2615	                        f"{list(task.dropoff)}"
2616	                    )
2617	            elif task.picked_up:
2618	                if robot.position != task.dropoff:
2619	                    raise ValueError(
2620	                        f"{label} has an empty remaining route with the goods "
2621	                        f"already picked up but the robot is at "
2622	                        f"{list(robot.position)}, not at the dropoff "
2623	                        f"{list(task.dropoff)}"
2624	                    )

2627	                    f"{label} has an empty remaining route before pickup: the "
2628	                    "task can only resume when the robot position, pickup "
2629	                    f"{list(task.pickup)} and dropoff {list(task.dropoff)} all "

2633	    @classmethod
2634	    def _iter_replay_events(
2635	        cls, data: Mapping[str, object]
2636	    ) -> Iterator[tuple[int, dict[str, object], object]]:
2637	        """Yield ``(index, frame, frame_type)`` for every replay event in order.
2638	
2639	        This is the single place that owns the ordinary-tick-frame rules both
2640	        format versions share, so they are never maintained twice: the
2641	        ``replay`` field must be a list, every frame must be an object, a
2642	        missing ``type`` means an ordinary tick frame, and tick frames must be
2643	        numbered consecutively from 1 -- map-change events sit between ticks
2644	        without consuming a number -- with a well-formed payload (checked via
2645	        the equally shared :meth:`_validate_tick_frame_payload`). Anything
2646	        beyond that stays with the two loaders: version 1 rejects non-tick
2647	        frames and normalizes the ``type`` field, version 2 keeps its own
2648	        event-type dispatch and map-change ordering checks. The scan is lazy,
2649	        so each frame is examined exactly when the consuming loader reaches it
2650	        and the first problem is reported in the same order as before.
2651	        """
2652	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "replay")
2653	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
2654	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'replay' must be a list")
2655	        tick_index = 0
2656	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
2657	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
2658	                raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} must be an object")
2659	            frame_type = frame.get("type", "tick")
2660	            if frame_type == "tick":
2661	                tick_index += 1
2662	                frame_tick = frame.get("tick")
2663	                if not _is_int(frame_tick):
2664	                    raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} field 'tick' must be an integer")
2665	                if frame_tick != tick_index:
2666	                    raise ValueError(
2667	                        "replay tick numbers must run consecutively from 1; frame "
2668	                        f"{index} has tick {frame_tick}, expected {tick_index}"
2669	                    )
2670	                cls._validate_tick_frame_payload(frame, frame_tick)
2671	            yield index, frame, frame_type

2673	    @classmethod
2674	    def _load_replay(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
2675	        replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
2676	        tick_index = 0
2677	        last_map_tick = -1
2678	        last_map_sequence = 0
2679	        for index, frame, frame_type in cls._iter_replay_events(data):
2680	            if frame_type == "tick":
2681	                tick_index += 1
2682	                replay.append(frame)
2683	            elif frame_type == "map_change":
2684	                tick = frame.get("tick")
2685	                sequence = frame.get("sequence")
2686	                if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
2687	                    raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} map change tick must be a non-negative integer")
2688	                if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
2689	                    raise ValueError(f"replay frame {index} map change sequence must be positive")
2690	                if tick != tick_index:
2691	                    raise ValueError(
2692	                        f"replay map change {sequence} is stamped tick {tick} but appears "
2693	                        f"after {tick_index} tick frames"
2694	                    )
2695	                if tick < last_map_tick or (
2696	                    tick == last_map_tick and sequence != last_map_sequence + 1
2697	                ):
2698	                    raise ValueError(
2699	                        f"replay map change {sequence} is out of order at tick {tick}"
2700	                    )
2701	                added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), f"replay frame {index}", "added")
2702	                removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), f"replay frame {index}", "removed")

2704	                    {
2705	                        "type": "map_change",
2706	                        "tick": tick,
2707	                        "sequence": sequence,
2708	                        "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
2709	                        "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
2710	                    }
2711	                )
2712	                last_map_tick = tick
2713	                last_map_sequence = sequence

2768	        Every tick frame is checked against the map in effect *during* that

2771	        between consecutive tick frames, two robots may not swap cells within
2772	        one tick, and ``moved`` must list exactly the robots whose positions
2773	        changed.

2775	        Version 2 map changes take effect after the tick they are stamped on,
2776	        in their recorded order: the frame for tick *t* is judged against the
2777	        base grid plus every change stamped below *t*, then the changes stamped
2778	        *t* are applied and may not add obstacles onto cells frame *t* shows a
2779	        robot on -- even when a later change of the same tick removes the cell
2780	        again. Tick-0 changes precede the first frame. Adjacency is always
2781	        judged between neighboring tick frames; a map change between them never
2782	        moves a robot.
2783	
2784	        Version 1 files pass no changes, so the saved grid governs every frame.
2785	        The first frame has no recorded predecessor: its cells, overlaps and
2786	        ``moved`` ids are still checked, but neither the distance of the first
2787	        moves nor the first ``moved`` list is second-guessed.
2788	        """

2790	        if len(tick_frames) != tick:

2792	                f"replay has {len(tick_frames)} tick frames but the checkpoint is at tick {tick}"
2793	            )

2802	                    f"replay frame {frame['tick']} robot ids do not match current robots"
2803	                )

2846	                obstacles.difference_update(
2847	                    {tuple(cell) for cell in change["removed"]}
2848	                )

2964	        finished by the end of that tick, not the tasks finished within it:

2966	        one frame, and a task once recorded must stay recorded in every later
2967	        frame -- a robot moving on to new work never erases the history. The
2968	        order inside a frame carries no meaning, and repeating the same task
2969	        across frames is the normal case. The last frame must therefore list

2974	        list must also be backed by a real delivery in that very frame: the

2977	        dropoff cell at that frame's end. Only the task's first-completion

1	"""History-plausibility checks for restored checkpoints.
2	
3	A checkpoint whose last frame matches the current state can still carry an
4	impossible past: robots out of bounds or sharing cells, teleports and swaps
5	between tick frames, ``moved`` lists that do not describe the frame, or robots
6	standing in cells that were obstacles at the time. ``load_checkpoint`` must
7	reject every such document while accepting everything the simulator itself
8	could produce, including traffic follow-moves and cells that close after a
9	robot has left them.
10	"""

13	import json
14	import os

24	        "tick": number,
25	        "moved": list(moved),
26	        "robots": {robot_id: list(cell) for robot_id, cell in positions.items()},
27	        "completed": list(completed),
28	    }
29

"""History-plausibility checks for restored checkpoints.

A checkpoint whose last frame matches the current state can still carry an
impossible past: robots out of bounds or sharing cells, teleports and swaps
between tick frames, ``moved`` lists that do not describe the frame, or robots
standing in cells that were obstacles at the time. ``load_checkpoint`` must
reject every such document while accepting everything the simulator itself
could produce, including traffic follow-moves and cells that close after a
robot has left them.
"""

import copy
import json
import os
import tempfile
import unittest

from warehouse_fleet import FleetSimulator, GridMap, Robot, Task


def tick_frame(number: int, moved, positions, completed=()):
    return {
        "type": "tick",
        "tick": number,
        "moved": list(moved),
        "robots": {robot_id: list(cell) for robot_id, cell in positions.items()},
        "completed": list(completed),
    }


def map_change(tick, sequence, added=(), removed=()):
    return {
        "type": "map_change",
        "tick": tick,
        "sequence": sequence,
        "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
        "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
    }


class HistoryDocumentBuilder:
    """Builds v1/v2 checkpoint docs around arbitrary replay histories.

    The starting document is a real zero-tick checkpoint, so every field not
    under test keeps a valid shape; routes and tasks stay empty.
    """

    def __init__(self, width=5, height=2, robots=(("A", (0, 0)), ("B", (4, 1)))):
        simulator = FleetSimulator(
            GridMap(width, height),
            [Robot(robot_id, position) for robot_id, position in robots],
            [],
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "state.json")
            simulator.save_checkpoint(path)
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                self.document = json.load(handle)
            self._tmp = tmpdir

    def frames(self, frames, *, base_obstacles=(), grid_obstacles=None):
        document = self.document
        document["tick"] = len(frames)
        document["replay"] = frames
        document["base_grid"]["obstacles"] = [list(cell) for cell in base_obstacles]
        document["grid"]["obstacles"] = (
            [list(cell) for cell in grid_obstacles]
            if grid_obstacles is not None
            else [list(cell) for cell in base_obstacles]
        )
        return self

    def dynamic(self, ordered_events, *, final_positions, base_obstacles=()):
        """ordered_events: replay frames/change records in storage order."""
        document = self.document
        tick_frames = [e for e in ordered_events if e["type"] == "tick"]
        changes = [e for e in ordered_events if e["type"] == "map_change"]
        document["tick"] = len(tick_frames)
        document["replay"] = copy.deepcopy(ordered_events)
        document["map_changes"] = [
            {key: copy.deepcopy(value) for key, value in event.items()}
            for event in changes
        ]
        document["base_grid"]["obstacles"] = [list(cell) for cell in base_obstacles]
        obstacles = set(base_obstacles)
        for event in changes:
            obstacles.update(tuple(cell) for cell in event["added"])
            obstacles.difference_update(tuple(cell) for cell in event["removed"])
        document["grid"]["obstacles"] = [list(cell) for cell in sorted(obstacles)]
        records = {record["robot_id"]: record for record in document["robots"]}
        for robot_id, cell in final_positions.items():
            records[robot_id]["position"] = list(cell)
            records[robot_id]["route"] = []
        return self

    def final(self, positions):
        records = {record["robot_id"]: record for record in self.document["robots"]}
        for robot_id, cell in positions.items():
            records[robot_id]["position"] = list(cell)
            records[robot_id]["route"] = []
        return self

    def version_one(self):
        document = self.document
        document["version"] = 1
        for key in ("base_grid", "map_changes", "paused_tasks", "traffic_waits"):
            document.pop(key, None)
        document["replay"] = [
            {key: value for key, value in frame.items() if key != "type"}
            for frame in document["replay"]
        ]
        return self

    def load(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "state.json")
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                json.dump(self.document, handle)
            return FleetSimulator.load_checkpoint(path)


def expect_rejected(testcase, document, fragment=None):
    with testcase.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
        _load(document)
    if fragment is not None:
        testcase.assertIn(fragment, str(context.exception))
    return str(context.exception)


def _load(document):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "state.json")
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(document, handle)
        return FleetSimulator.load_checkpoint(path)

        self.builder = HistoryDocumentBuilder()

    def reject(self, document, fragment=None):
